criteria.text: User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

criteria.text: User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

System state: The user has open chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay on the Chore List marked “Unassigned.” Any housemate can assign an unassigned chore, the same as a first assignment (see SCRUM-6).
System state: The user has completed chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay in the household’s chore history with the user’s name.

System state: The user is the household manager. Expected System Behavior: The role passes on following the SCRUM-62 rules: the next highest nominee is invited, or the household returns to the no-manager state.
System state: The user has voted or been nominated for household manager. Expected System Behavior: Their vote and any votes for them are cleared.
System state: The user leaves. Expected System Behavior: Remaining housemates are notified: “[Name] left the household.” The user no longer appears in the House tab roster or the “Assigned to” list.

System state: The user is the only member of the household. Expected System Behavior: The confirmation instead reads: “You’re the last member of [Household name]. Leaving will delete the household and all of its chores.” Confirming deletes the household.
User Action: A former member opens a new invite link to the same household. Expected System Behavior: They can rejoin as a new member. Their past completed chores remain in history.
Error Condition: Leaving fails. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.” The user stays in the household.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

Error Condition: The preferences fail to save. Expected message: The system displays an error message and provides an option to try saving again. Prototype: {Link}

User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.

criteria.text: User Action: Clicks “Leave household” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A confirmation appears: “Leave [Household name]? Your open chores will become unassigned.” with “Leave” and “Cancel.”
User Action: Clicks “Cancel.” Expected System Behavior: The confirmation closes, and nothing changes.
User Action: Clicks “Leave.” Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the household, and the “Your household” screen opens with options to create or join a household.

System state: The user has open chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay on the Chore List marked “Unassigned.” Any housemate can assign an unassigned chore, the same as a first assignment (see SCRUM-6).
System state: The user has completed chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay in the household’s chore history with the user’s name.

System state: The user is the household manager. Expected System Behavior: The role passes on following the SCRUM-62 rules: the next highest nominee is invited, or the household returns to the no-manager state.
System state: The user has voted or been nominated for household manager. Expected System Behavior: Their vote and any votes for them are cleared.
System state: The user leaves. Expected System Behavior: Remaining housemates are notified: “[Name] left the household.” The user no longer appears in the House tab roster or the “Assigned to” list.

System state: The user is the only member of the household. Expected System Behavior: The confirmation instead reads: “You’re the last member of [Household name]. Leaving will delete the household and all of its chores.” Confirming deletes the household.
User Action: A former member opens a new invite link to the same household. Expected System Behavior: They can rejoin as a new member. Their past completed chores remain in history.
Error Condition: Leaving fails. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.” The user stays in the household.

criteria.text: User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by most open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
criteria.note: Jira says “sorted by fewest open chores”; the team chose most open chores first (Anthony, 2026-11-22; README Conflicts row 48). A housemate prefers a chore when its Category is one of their chore types (README Conflicts rows 46 and 51).

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.

Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

criteria.text: User Action: Clicks “Leave household” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A confirmation appears: “Leave [Household name]? Your open chores will become unassigned.” with “Leave” and “Cancel.”
User Action: Clicks “Cancel.” Expected System Behavior: The confirmation closes, and nothing changes.
User Action: Clicks “Leave.” Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the household, and the “Your household” screen opens with options to create or join a household.

System state: The user has open chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay on the Chore List marked “Unassigned.” Any housemate can assign an unassigned chore, the same as a first assignment (see SCRUM-6).
System state: The user has completed chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay in the household’s chore history with the user’s name.

System state: The user is the household manager. Expected System Behavior: The role passes on following the SCRUM-62 rules: the next highest nominee is invited, or the household returns to the no-manager state.
System state: The user has voted or been nominated for household manager. Expected System Behavior: Their vote and any votes for them are cleared.
System state: The user leaves. Expected System Behavior: Remaining housemates are notified: “[Name] left the household.” The user no longer appears in the House tab roster or the “Assigned to” list.

System state: The user is the only member of the household. Expected System Behavior: The confirmation instead reads: “You’re the last member of [Household name]. Leaving will delete the household and all of its chores.” Confirming deletes the household.
User Action: A former member opens a new invite link to the same household. Expected System Behavior: They can rejoin as a new member. Their past completed chores remain in history.
Error Condition: Leaving fails. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.” The user stays in the household.

criteria.text: User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

criteria.text: User Action: Clicks “Leave household” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A confirmation appears: “Leave [Household name]? Your open chores will become unassigned.” with “Leave” and “Cancel.”
User Action: Clicks “Cancel.” Expected System Behavior: The confirmation closes, and nothing changes.
User Action: Clicks “Leave.” Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the household, and the “Your household” screen opens with options to create or join a household.

System state: The user has open chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay on the Chore List marked “Unassigned.” Any housemate can assign an unassigned chore, the same as a first assignment (see SCRUM-6).
System state: The user has completed chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay in the household’s chore history with the user’s name.

System state: The user is the household manager. Expected System Behavior: The role passes on following the SCRUM-62 rules: the next highest nominee is invited, or the household returns to the no-manager state.
System state: The user has voted or been nominated for household manager. Expected System Behavior: Their vote and any votes for them are cleared.
System state: The user leaves. Expected System Behavior: Remaining housemates are notified: “[Name] left the household.” The user no longer appears in the House tab roster or the “Assigned to” list.

System state: The user is the only member of the household. Expected System Behavior: The confirmation instead reads: “You’re the last member of [Household name]. Leaving will delete the household and all of its chores.” Confirming deletes the household.
User Action: A former member opens a new invite link to the same household. Expected System Behavior: They can rejoin as a new member. Their past completed chores remain in history.
Error Condition: Leaving fails. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.” The user stays in the household.

criteria.text: User Action: User navigates to their chore preferences. Expected System Behavior: Displays the household’s chores, each with an option to mark it as preferred.
User Action: User marks or unmarks chores as preferred and saves. Expected System Behavior: The preferences are saved, and a confirmation message is displayed.
User Action: A housemate assigns a chore. Expected System Behavior: Housemates who prefer that chore are shown as preferring it in the assignment options.
Error Condition: The household has no chores yet. Expected message: “No chores to choose from yet.”
Error Condition: The preferences fail to save. Expected message: The system displays an error message and provides an option to try saving again. Prototype: {Link}

User Action: Opens “Nominate household manager” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: A list opens of housemates who are open to nomination. The user selects one, and their vote is saved. Each housemate has one vote and can change it at any time.
User Action: Turns off “Open to nomination” on their own profile page. Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the nomination list, and any votes for them are cleared.

System state: There is no household manager, and one housemate has the most votes. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives a notification inviting them to become household manager. A “Become household manager” button appears on their profile page and in the House tab.

System state: There is a household manager, and another housemate has more votes than the manager. Expected System Behavior: That housemate receives the same invitation and button. The current manager keeps the role until the invitation is accepted.
System state: A housemate ties the current household manager in votes. Expected System Behavior: No invitation is sent. The current manager keeps the role.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Become household manager.” Expected System Behavior: They become household manager. The previous manager, if any, loses the role and is notified. A “Household manager” chip appears next to the new manager’s name in the House tab, and all housemates are notified.

User Action: The invited housemate clicks “Decline.” Expected System Behavior: With no current manager, the next highest nominee receives the invitation. With a current manager, the current manager keeps the role.

System state: Two or more housemates are tied for the most votes, and there is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every tied housemate receives the invitation. The first to accept becomes household manager.

System state: There is no household manager. Expected System Behavior: Every housemate sees a “Become household manager” button on their profile page and in the House tab. Clicking it makes them household manager.

User Action: The household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: An “Edit” button opens an “Edit chore” screen with the same fields as “Add chore,” prefilled, including “Assigned to.” Saving updates the chore for all housemates. If the chore was reassigned, the new and previous assignees are notified.

System state: A housemate who is not the household manager opens Chore Details. Expected System Behavior: No “Edit” button is shown. Any housemate can still add a chore and choose its first assignee (see SCRUM-6).
User Action: The household manager clicks “Step down” in the House tab. Expected System Behavior: They are no longer household manager, and the top remaining nominee receives the invitation.
Error Condition: There is no household manager and no nominations. Message: “No Household Manager assigned. Claim role in House tab.”

Error Condition: The household manager leaves the household (see SCRUM-75) or deletes their account. Expected behavior: The next highest nominee receives the invitation. If there are no nominees, the household returns to the no-manager state.
Error Condition: A vote, role change or chore edit fails to save. Message: “Something went wrong. Please try again.”

User Action: Opens a housemate’s profile from the House tab. Expected System Behavior: A “Preferred chores” section lists the chores that housemate marked as preferred (see SCRUM-61), in alphabetical order. The section is view only.
User Action: Opens their own profile. Expected System Behavior: The “Preferred chores” section shows their own preferences with an “Edit preferences” link.
User Action: Clicks “Edit preferences.” Expected System Behavior: The chore preferences screen from SCRUM-61 opens. After saving, the profile shows the updated list.
System state: A housemate updates their preferences. Expected System Behavior: The change appears on their profile for all housemates.
System state: A preferred chore is deleted from the household. Expected System Behavior: It no longer appears in anyone’s preferred chores.
Error Condition: A housemate has no preferred chores. Message: “[Name] hasn’t picked any preferred chores yet.”
Error Condition: The user has no preferred chores on their own profile. Message: “You haven’t picked any preferred chores yet.” with a “Set preferences” link.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Message: “We couldn’t load preferred chores. Please try again.” with a “Retry” button.

User Action: Opens “Assigned to” on the “Add chore” or “Edit chore” screen for a chore that one or more housemates prefer. Expected System Behavior: Those housemates appear at the top of the list under “Suggested,” each labeled “Prefers this chore” with their number of open chores. Suggested housemates are sorted by fewest open chores. All other housemates appear below under “Everyone else.”
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” for a chore no one prefers. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates with no “Suggested” section.
User Action: Opens “Assigned to” before entering a chore name. Expected System Behavior: The list shows all housemates. Suggestions appear once a chore name is entered.
User Action: Changes the chore name after opening “Assigned to.” Expected System Behavior: The suggestions update to match the new name.
User Action: Selects any housemate, suggested or not. Expected System Behavior: The chore is assigned to that housemate. Suggestions never block a choice.
System state: A housemate who prefers the chore has left the household. Expected System Behavior: They do not appear in suggestions.
Error Condition: Preferences fail to load. Expected behavior: The list shows all housemates as normal, with the message “Suggestions aren’t available right now.” Assignment still works.

User Action: Clicks “Leave.” Expected System Behavior: The user is removed from the household, and the “Your household” screen opens with options to create or join a household.

System state: The user has open chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay on the Chore List marked “Unassigned.” Any housemate can assign an unassigned chore, the same as a first assignment (see SCRUM-6).
System state: The user has completed chores when they leave. Expected System Behavior: Those chores stay in the household’s chore history with the user’s name.

System state: The user is the household manager. Expected System Behavior: The role passes on following the SCRUM-62 rules: the next highest nominee is invited, or the household returns to the no-manager state.

System state: The user leaves. Expected System Behavior: Remaining housemates are notified: “[Name] left the household.” The user no longer appears in the House tab roster or the “Assigned to” list.

System state: The user is the only member of the household. Expected System Behavior: The confirmation instead reads: “You’re the last member of [Household name]. Leaving will delete the household and all of its chores.” Confirming deletes the household.
User Action: A former member opens a new invite link to the same household. Expected System Behavior: They can rejoin as a new member. Their past completed chores remain in history.
